description: Compare lifetime monthly pension payments against a lump-sum offer growing at an assumed return, with the break-even age.

faqs.a: Lifetime pension total = monthly pension × 12 × (life expectancy − start age). Lump-sum future value = offer × (1 + return)^years.
faqs.q: How are the two totals compared?

faqs.a: The break-even age is where the growing lump sum catches up with cumulative pension payments — solved by iterating year by year.
faqs.q: How is the break-even age found?

faqs.a: A pension is guaranteed income for life; a lump sum gives control and inheritance options but carries investment and longevity risk. Weigh both, not just the totals.
faqs.q: Which is better — pension or lump sum?
